Moraga.headline: The storm eases Friday, but another round of rain is possible Tuesday
Moraga.text: The main cold-core system is still close enough to keep Moraga unsettled into Thursday, even with the strongest frontal rain already moving through. The NWS expects the surface low to cross Thursday morning, bringing another opportunity for heavy showers, isolated thunderstorms and small hail before the activity gradually becomes more showery. The local model blend adds about six-tenths of an inch Thursday, but the timing and placement of heavier cells will determine the neighborhood total. Showers should taper Thursday afternoon and evening, with a few lingering into early Friday. Behind the low, colder air settles in; Friday and Saturday mornings could be chilly, although cloud cover will make a meaningful difference to the low. A weaker front approaches Saturday and may bring occasional showers into Sunday, but NWS guidance indicates substantially less rain than this week's storm. Monday looks like a relative break. Ensemble guidance then points to a renewed, potentially wetter system around Tuesday, though details remain uncertain this far out.

Lafayette.headline: Thursday's showers gradually fade before a potentially wetter Tuesday system
Lafayette.text: Reliez Valley remains under the influence of the departing storm Thursday, with the surface low forecast to move through in the morning. That keeps the door open for another round of heavy showers and perhaps an isolated thunderstorm before rain becomes more scattered later in the day. The local ensemble blend is near six-tenths of an inch for Thursday, although localized totals will depend on where the heavier bands track. Showers may linger into early Friday, then colder air filters into the East Bay valleys. Friday and Saturday mornings look chilly, but cloud cover could keep temperatures from dropping as much as the clearer model solutions suggest. A new front approaches Saturday and may bring some rain into Sunday; the NWS expects this system to be notably weaker than the current storm. Monday appears to offer the best chance for a quieter day. Looking farther ahead, EPS and GEFS guidance both strengthen the rain signal around Tuesday. That is worth watching, but exact timing and amounts are not yet dependable.

Danville.headline: A final burst of showers Thursday, then a quieter stretch before Tuesday
Danville.text: The storm's center is forecast to move across the region Thursday morning, so Sycamore Valley should not assume the rain is finished just because the main frontal band has passed. The NWS continues to flag the potential for heavy showers, isolated thunderstorms and small hail with the colder air wrapping around the low. The local model blend carries roughly three-quarters of an inch for Thursday, with neighborhood totals sensitive to where the more persistent showers set up. Rain should gradually become more scattered Thursday afternoon and evening, with a few showers possibly hanging on into early Friday. Colder air follows, making Friday and Saturday mornings feel distinctly wintry for the East Bay valleys, though clouds may limit the overnight chill. Another front approaches Saturday and could bring spotty rain through Sunday, but the NWS expects much less precipitation than this week's system. Monday looks comparatively quiet. Ensemble guidance then signals a renewed wet pattern around Tuesday, although confidence in the exact track and rainfall amount remains limited.

Greenbrook.headline: Thursday showers taper, while the next significant rain signal shifts to Tuesday
Greenbrook.text: Greenbrook remains close to the departing storm's circulation Thursday, and the next surface-low passage is forecast for the morning. That means another period of heavy showers is possible, with a small chance of thunder and hail as colder air moves overhead. The local model blend is around eight-tenths of an inch for Thursday, a little higher than the nearby Danville guidance, but that difference should not be treated as a precise neighborhood-scale prediction. Showers should become more scattered Thursday afternoon and evening, then gradually wind down into early Friday. Colder air settles in behind the system, bringing chilly Friday and Saturday mornings; cloud cover will be the main factor controlling how low temperatures fall. A weaker front approaches Saturday and may produce occasional showers into Sunday, though the NWS expects this round to be much lighter than the current storm. Monday looks like a relative lull. The extended ensemble signal strengthens again around Tuesday, suggesting another wet system may be approaching, but its details remain uncertain.
